subject: Surprise early-cycle invoice INV-2026-11-1149: unexpected metering spike and VAT question
messages:
From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@atlaslabs.io>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com; Atlas Labs Finance <finance@atlaslabs.io>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0500
Subject: Surprise early-cycle invoice INV-2026-11-1149 — usage spike & VAT question

Hi Grace,

We just opened our invoice for Nov and saw a charge we weren't expecting: INV-2026-11-1149 for $18,540 (posted 2026-11-14). The token count on the invoice looks ~2x what our internal telemetry shows for the same window. I attached an export from our side (usage_export_20261114.csv) showing request IDs and timestamps for the 02:00–03:00 UTC window where most of the delta sits.

Two quick asks:
- Can you provide a token-level breakdown for the invoice (per-request or per-session) so we can map to our logs?
- How will Redwood handle VAT on any retroactive credit? We need documentation for our reclaim/tax team.

This is time-sensitive — finance is flagging the invoice for payment hold if we can't reconcile quickly. Please advise next steps and whether you can pause collection while you investigate.

Thanks,
Ava Collins
Head of Platform, Atlas Labs
ava.collins@atlaslabs.io
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: usage_export_20261114.csv
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Surprise early-cycle invoice INV-2026-11-1149 — usage spike & VAT question

Hi Ava — thanks for the heads-up and for attaching your export. Sorry for the surprise here; we’ll prioritize this.

Immediate plan (proposed):
1) I will open a billing investigation and request a raw token export for the billing window from the metering service.
2) Ben (billing) will do a quick triage to look for duplication/replay patterns.
3) Kimberly (tax) will confirm VAT/tax treatment if we issue a credit.
4) We can put the invoice into a temporary collection hold while we validate — please confirm you want us to do that.

Initial hypothesis: we're seeing cases where a streaming client fallback triggered a retry path in our gateway that resulted in duplicate stream segments being counted as separate requests. That can look like duplicated tokens in a short window. I don’t want to commit until Ben has the exports.

Ben/Kimberly — looping you in to lead the investigation and coordinate a provisional credit if appropriate. Ben, can you scope the delta and suggest a conservative provisional credit amount we can apply this week?

Ava — can you also send a quick example request-id from your CSV (one line) so we can lookup the session trace in our logs?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Surprise early-cycle invoice INV-2026-11-1149 — quick triage findings

Hi all — I ran a preliminary aggregation against the metering export for the 2026-11-14 billing slice and compared it to the CSV Ava shared. Notes below:

Summary:
- We see a concentrated spike between 02:06–02:48 UTC. During that interval the billing system counted ~2.08x more tokens than the client-side extract.
- The majority of the extra tokens map to a small set of session prefixes (session-7f4b*). Those session IDs show repeated open/close patterns consistent with a streaming fallback retry.
- No evidence of a wholesale ratecard misconfiguration. This appears to be duplicated counting for retransmitted segments.

Conservative remediation proposal:
1) Apply a provisional credit equal to the duplicated portion we can confidently attribute to retries (estimate: 42,400 tokens ≈ $2,420). We will treat this as provisional while our forensic logs complete.
2) Post an adjusted invoice and a credit note that includes VAT adjustments where applicable. Kimberly will advise on VAT flow.
3) If the forensics expand the scope, we will adjust the credit retroactively.

Attachments: billing_trace_20261114.xlsx (breakdown by request ID and token buckets). Full forensic export is in the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/records/INV-2026-11-1149-analysis

Ava — please confirm you want us to apply the provisional credit now. If finance prefers a formal credit note or DocuSign acknowledgement for their records, we can generate that.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Billing Analyst — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks for confirming. We will:
1) Post the provisional credit of $2,420 to your account today and generate a credit note referencing INV-2026-11-1149.
2) Issue an adjusted invoice that nets the credit and shows the VAT recalculation. Because you supplied a UK VAT registration (GB999888777), the credit note will show the VAT reversal consistent with UK VAT rules.
3) No DocuSign required — we will issue standard accounting documents (credit note + corrected invoice) and email PDFs to finance@atlaslabs.io within 3 business days.
